Matrix expressions

Source: R/matrices-expr.R
matrix-expressions.Rd

MatrixSymbol(name, n, m) is a symbolic n by m matrix. Identity(n), ZeroMatrix(m, n) and OneMatrix(m, n) are the special matrices. +, -, * and ^ build the canonical MatAdd, MatMul and MatPow (like terms combine, identities and zeros simplify, shapes are checked and mismatches raise a ShapeError). t() transposes and distributes; Transpose(), Inverse() and Adjoint() build unevaluated nodes (A^-1 is Inverse(A)). Trace(), Determinant() and Permanent() are scalar functions of a matrix; doit() applies their rules. MatrixElement(A, i, j) is the entry with SymPy's zero based indices. as_explicit() turns an expression with integer shape into an explicit Matrix(). mat_shape() gives the shape and matrix_symbols() the matrix symbols.

Usage

MatrixSymbol(name, n, m)

Identity(n)

ZeroMatrix(n, m)

OneMatrix(n, m)

mat_shape(e)

MatMul(..., evaluate = FALSE)

MatAdd(..., evaluate = FALSE)

MatPow(A, k)

Transpose(A)

Inverse(A)

Adjoint(A)

Trace(A)

Determinant(A)

Permanent(A)

HadamardProduct(..., evaluate = FALSE)

HadamardPower(A, k)

KroneckerProduct(...)

MatrixElement(A, i, j)

FunctionMatrix(n, m, f)

DiagMatrix(A)

diagonalize_vector(A)

DiagonalOf(A)

DiagonalMatrix(A)

PermutationMatrix(perm)

MatrixPermute(A, perm, axis = 0)

DotProduct(A, B)

MatrixSlice(A, rowslice, colslice)

blockcut(A, rowsizes, colsizes)

BlockMatrix(blocks)

BlockDiagMatrix(...)

block_collapse(e)

matrix_symbols(e)

as_explicit(e)

Arguments

name

The name.

n, m

Dimensions.

e, A, B

A matrix expression.

...

Matrices, or for MatMul() matrices and scalars.

evaluate

If TRUE, MatAdd() and MatMul() put their arguments in canonical form, as doit() does; by default they keep them as given, as in SymPy. A MatMul() of scalars only is their product.

k

An exponent.

i, j

Zero based indices.

f

A Lambda() of two variables giving the entries.

perm

A Permutation() or a vector of zero based images.

axis

0 to permute rows, 1 for columns.

rowslice, colslice

A zero based index, c(start, stop) or c(start, stop, step); NA (or NULL in a list) takes the default end, and negative values count from the end, as Python slices.

rowsizes, colsizes

Block sizes along rows and columns.

blocks

A list of rows, each a list of matrices.

Value

A matrix expression, a scalar expression or an explicit matrix.

Examples

A <- MatrixSymbol("A", 2, 2); B <- MatrixSymbol("B", 2, 2)
A * B + A * B
#> 2*A*B
t(A * B)
#> B.T*A.T
A^-1 * A
#> I
as_explicit(A * B)
#> Matrix(2, 2)
#> [A[0, 0]*B[0, 0] + A[0, 1]*B[1, 0], A[0, 0]*B[0, 1] + A[0, 1]*B[1, 1]]
#> [A[1, 0]*B[0, 0] + A[1, 1]*B[1, 0], A[1, 0]*B[0, 1] + A[1, 1]*B[1, 1]]
doit(Trace(A + B))
#> Trace(A) + Trace(B)
